Subject: Follow-up: streaming behavior & eval artifacts for Orion HealthTech POC

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive demo earlier. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we’re aligned on the streaming issues you called out (partial outputs, stop-sequence behavior, and occasional latency spikes):

Call recap
- Observed behavior: model sometimes emits truncated clauses mid-sentence when streaming (appears ~5-8% of prompts in our quick sample).
- Stop sequences: some of your task prompts rely on custom separators ("---end---") and we saw the generator occasionally ignore the separator or cut right before it.
- Latency: most tokens stream within the SLA, but there are intermittent spikes (200-400ms extra) on longer context windows.

Attached to this thread I’ve included:
- orion_streaming_prompts_v1.txt — the prompt set we captured during the call (small, reproducible examples).
- orion_latency_benchmarks.csv — a short run from a dedicated 13B instance we used to reproduce timing.
- model_suggestions.pdf — quick model-fit notes and quantization trade-offs.

Proposed next steps (action items)
1) Daniel / Priya: please run the attached prompt set against your sandbox and paste two short examples of where the stream truncated unexpectedly. Paste the raw HTTP streaming frames if possible. (Due: Feb 12 PST)
2) Internal (Neha / Monica / Jordan): we’ll run the prompts against 3 candidate variants and surface a short diffs doc (due Feb 12 EOD).
3) Small follow-up sync (15m) to align on whether stop-sequence enforcement or tokenization tweaks are the cause — I’ll propose times after we get the examples.

Why we think this might be fixable without model swap
- Preliminary hypothesis: stop-sequence handling + streaming buffer flush thresholds. In some cases the server-side buffer flushes mid-token boundary when a custom stop pattern overlaps a subword boundary — that can look like truncation.

Let me know if you’d like us to spin up a dedicated variant for you to test more broadly. I can also share a small eval harness (simple Node script) that reproduces the streaming frames.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Thanks Jordan — attaching a short reproduction and a paste of the streaming frames we captured from our sandbox. Below is one problematic example (we ran exactly the prompt in orion_streaming_prompts_v1.txt — example #3).

--- raw streaming frames (abbreviated) ---
frame 1: {"delta":"Our diagnostic indicates that the patient"}
frame 2: {"delta":" has elevated creatinine,"}
frame 3: {"delta":" and we recommend a follow-"}
frame 4: {"delta":" up with nephrology."}
frame 5: {"delta":"\n"}
frame 6: {"delta":""}  <-- here it stopped; expected: "follow-up appointment scheduled for next week.---end---"

Observation: you can see the generator finished a middle-of-phrase token ("follow-") then resumed to complete with "up" in the following frame, but in our instability cases the stream terminates entirely before the final clause.

Also attached a quick log showing a 320ms spike on token batch 12 (timestamped). We’ll run the rest of the prompt set and send any other examples we find.

Question for your team: do you want the raw trace (we can share a gzipped HAR) or is the pasted frame snippet sufficient to start root-causing?

—Daniel

Thanks for the snippet, Daniel — this is exactly the kind of trace we need. Quick responses + what we ran internally: 

What we reproduced
- We ran example #3 against three variants: rw-open-7b (fp16), rw-open-7b-int8, and rw-nova-13b (fp16). The truncated-frame behavior reproduced on the smaller variant ~6% of runs, and ~1% on nova-13b.

Immediate mitigations (short tests you can run this afternoon)
- Stop-sequence enforcement: add an explicit newline + sentinel (e.g., "\n---END---") as the stop pattern to avoid subword overlap. Example: replace "---end---" with "\n---END---" in the prompt set.
- Streaming buffer config: increase flush threshold to 48 bytes or set flush-on-complete-token=true in the client wrapper. We’ve attached a one-page note in model_suggestions.pdf showing how to configure buffers for Node and Python clients.

Recommended model candidates for POC
- rw-nova-13b (fp16): best quality / low truncation rate (recommended for critical clinical QA flows).
- rw-open-7b-int8: similar latency and cost savings; acceptable if you can enforce the newline sentinel.

Benchmarks we attached
- orion_latency_benchmarks.csv — token latency distribution for the three variants (short run).
- model_suggestions.pdf — trade-offs and a suggested A/B plan (canary nova-13b for high-criticality routes, open-7b-int8 for lower-cost inference).

Next steps (we’ll take these on our side)
- Neha / Monica: we’ll prepare a short eval doc with per-prompt pass/fail for both stop sequence and sentence-complete checks.
- Daniel: if you can confirm whether you prefer the newline sentinel change, we’ll push an updated prompt set and re-run the full 500-sample run on a dedicated instance.

I’m available for a 15m sync tomorrow (Feb 13) 08:30–11:30 PT or 14:00–16:00 PT — will drop a calendar invite when you confirm a window.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
